stories.summary: Wipe the blood off your fangs as Rebel Wolves are readying Update 1.2 for The Blood of Dawnwalker, bringing new features. The post The Blood of Dawnwalker Update 1.2 Adds New Game+ & Gameplay Balance Changes appeared first on Insider Gaming .

sources.name: Insider Gaming
sources.title: The Blood of Dawnwalker Update 1.2 Adds New Game+ & Gameplay Balance Changes
sources.text: The Blood of Dawnwalker has kickstarted a new franchise, and the debut game is only getting bigger and better, thanks to new game modes and changes in the 1.2 update. Nearly a month on from Blood of Dawnwalker’s Update 1.1 , the second major patch has been announced. If you’ve finished the game and want to carry on, the incoming New Game Plus option will add plenty of longevity to The Blood of Dawnwalker . ‘New features’ and ‘Changes and improvements’ are at the heart of The Blood of Dawnwalker’s Update 1.2. From 1.2, you’ll be able to enjoy New Game+, which you can ‘dive straight into’ once you’ve completed the epilogue. Levels, skills, and inventory items carry over, and the level cap is raised to Level 100. Most items will have New Game Plus variations, offering new stats and ways to play. More songs are being added to the game’s soundtrack, and the update announcement reveals the OST is en route to ‘Spotify and other streaming services soon!’ Finally, some pretty significant gameplay changes are happening. Enemy health pools and ability usage are being reworked, and the game’s map has been upgraded to be smoother all-around. The Blood of Dawnwalker has already sold 1 million copies , and updates like this should only justify that purchase more. How are you finding The Blood of Dawnwalker? Let us know your thoughts via the free Insider Gaming Discord server . sources.name: GamesRadar
sources.title: The Blood of Dawnwalker is getting New Game+ next week
sources.text: "If you completed the Epilogue, you can dive right back into Vale Sangora with New Game+" Rebel Wolves has confirmed that The Blood of Dawnwalker is getting New Game+ as part of its 1.2 update next week. Despite a number of nominations and bringing out one of the best vampire games of the modern era , The Blood of Dawnwalker didn't pick up any awards at the Golden Joystick Awards this week. It did come close, with a second place finish in PC Game of the Year and Best Storytelling, and a fifth place finish in Ultimate Game of the Year. The ex- CD Projekt Red devs at Rebel Wolves were happy with their performance , and clearly haven't let the narrow losses faze them, as the game's next major patch is coming very soon. As announced by Rebel Wolves on Reddit , The Blood of Dawnwalker 1.2 update releases next week. This update will include balance changes with enemy health pools and ability use being tweaked as well as terrain adjustments to improve movement around the world. But the headline act of this new update is New Game+ finally arriving in the game. "If you completed the Epilogue, you can dive right back into Vale Sangora with New Game+." the post reads. As part of this mode, the level cap is being raised to 100, with enemies balanced and scaled accordingly. On top of that, items will receive New Game+ versions with updated stats, too. The average playthrough of The Blood of Dawnwalker is around 25 hours according to HowLongToBeat , so this new addition should help you get even more out of what is considered "short" by RPG standards. 6 things I need from The Blood of Dawnwalker's sequel. sources.name: Polygon
sources.title: Blood of Dawnwalker Finally Gets Its Most Requested Feature Next Week
sources.text: Rebel Wolves is giving fans what they’ve been asking for in update 1.2 It's been just over two months since The Blood of Dawnwalker was released and fans have been clamoring for one missing feature for basically that long. Now developer Rebel Wolves is set to appease that demand with the upcoming update 1.2. Yes, New Game Plus is going to be a reality for the vampire RPG. Rebel Wolves has already pushed several post-release updates to The Blood of Dawnwalker to address fan feedback. The game's first big patch, update 1.1 , added a new difficulty mode, tweaked combat, and introduced the all-important ability to pet animals. It crucially lacked New Game Plus. Back in September, director Konrad Tomaszkiewicz revealed that the studio was exploring the possibility but didn't want to speak about it yet. Staying tight-lipped was likely meant to not overexcite fans if the feature couldn't actually be delivered. Well, now it seems like Rebel Wolves has figured it out. As revealed on the game's social media accounts , New Game Plus will be added as part of update 1.2. The big patch will be released next week. A specific date was not shared, but update 1.1 was dropped on a Thursday. As detailed by the announcement, New Game Plus will be available once players have completed the game's epilogue. Your level, skills, and inventory will all carry over. Additionally, the level cap will be raised to 100 and enemies will be balanced and scaled across all regions. Items will be given New Game Plus versions with updated stats. Enjoy sinking your teeth back into Vale Sangora. New Game Plus isn't the only new feature coming to the game in update 1.2, though it is the biggest addition. If you purchased The Blood of Dawnwalker — Eclipse Edition , you'll notice that the in-game soundtrack will be extended with new songs. Streaming services will also get the new soundtrack material soon. As for general tweaks to The Blood of Dawnwalker , update 1.2 will make some balance changes to enemy health pools and how often they use their abilities during combat. Some terrain geometry has also been adjusted to allow for smoother movement during combat and exploration. The Blood of Dawnwalker has been one of 2026's great surprises, but it is unclear whether it will be able to shine through a crowded field as awards season kicks into full gear.

sources.name: Eurogamer
sources.title: The Blood of Dawnwalker is getting a New Game Plus mode in next week's update
sources.text: A New Game Plus mode is coming to vampiric RPG The Blood of Dawnwalker next week. Developer Rebel Wolves has now detailed everything coming with The Blood of Dawnwalker's Update 1.2, currently planned to go live sometime next week, and top of the list of changes is a New Game Plus for players who have already rolled credits on the game. "If you completed the Epilogue, you can dive right back into Vale Sangora with New Game+," the developer revealed earlier today. "Your level, skills, and inventory will carry over." Rebel Wolves is upping the level cap to 100 for New Game Plus, which will also have items with updated stats and enemies "balanced and scaled uniformly across all regions." Elsewhere in Update 1.2, the studio is making tweaks to "enemy health pools and how often they use their abilities during combat," and improving terrain geometry to allow for "smoother movement during combat and exploration." We'll need to wait for more comprehensive patch notes before finding out which enemies are getting spongier or flimsier, however. While the incoming patch doesn't seem to be as beefy as the last - the one that added animal petting and an easier Story mode - it'll be a good way to sink your teeth deeper into a game that's already begging to be replayed, thanks to a time management mechanic that can drastically change any given run. The new game from some former The Witcher 3 veterans came out in September and seems to have been a hit. Eurogamer's The Blood of Dawnwalker review called the game a "familiar dark fantasy adventure, but one with bold and provocative ideas of its own, that's mostly, enormously successful."

sources.name: PlayStation Blog
sources.title: Vindictus: Defying Fate comes to PS5 next year
sources.text: Discover the world and core gameplay of Vindictus: Defying Fate. Hello, PlayStation players. I’m Dongseok Oh, lead director of the high-octane action-RPG Vindictus: Defying Fate . Our team is building a medieval fantasy adventure where heroes must stand against colossal foes in a world inspired by Celtic mythology and, today, we’re officially revealing that Vindictus: Defying Fate is coming to PS5. I’m honored to have this opportunity to introduce the core gameplay and world to the PlayStation community. Visceral, engaging combat is key to the Vindictus: Defying Fate experience. So much so, that weapons are the first step when we conceptualize our heroes. We carefully consider a wide range of weapons, from familiar ones players expect to see to more unconventional options that offer unique and exciting combat possibilities, and choose one as the foundation. Our teams behind narrative, combat actions, and appearance are given freedom to explore their own designs and express their creativity before the overall direction is established, crafting a hero with a distinct combat style. Who you choose to play will yield an entirely different experience. You can devote yourself to the one hero who captures your heart, or develop several heroes and choose the right one as the situation demands. Lann: Relies on dodging rather than guarding. Chain dodges to avoid attacks, then close in for a strike immediately after landing a hit. Fiona: Uses her shield to block and counterattack, balancing offense and defense. Deflect an enemy attack with precise timing to continue your own attack without interruption. If you hope to withstand combat in this harsh world, you will need intense focus and precise control. Survival means learning how your enemies move. Depending on your chosen hero’s abilities, you can parry a crushing blow, block a brutal barrage of attacks, or dodge at just the right moment. The key is to create an opening and strike back with a heavy counterattack. Delia: Builds up power to unleash a devastating blow. She can also evade attacks by piercing through an enemy as she strikes. Karok: Absorbs the impact of incoming attacks to stand his ground. Time your response to a powerful enemy attack to enter a contest of strength. You also craft your own weapons, customizing your outfits and appearance to make your hero uniquely yours. “The gates of paradise shall open when one race eradicates the other.” Ruled by this fateful prophecy, the Humans and Fomors of Taranúil have long soaked the land in each other’s blood. You must face your fate as a new recruit of the Kalbram Mercenaries, working under the Rocheste Order. As you set out on your journey, you’ll uncover a shadowy plot hiding beneath old conflicts. As you explore the world of Vindictus, you’ll encounter breathtaking lands still touched by the breath of ancient gods, and thriving centers of human culture that have blossomed even amid war. Every step across this uncharted continent reveals a new landscape, yet the same reality awaits: war against the Fomors. From Fomors hostile to humankind to ferocious beasts, all manner of enemies lie in wait. Colhen: A small farming village on the front line, where human and Fomor territories meet. Northern Ruins: Ancient ruins that once stood in neutral territory between humans and Fomors. Hoarfrost Hollow: A valley of snow-covered forests, ice mines, and glacial waterfalls. Ainle: A city destroyed overnight by a mysterious incident. This journey is, at its core, one you walk alone. We are also preparing multiplayer content that will let you face overwhelming threats alongside other players. Defy your fate The prophecy has already been spoken. Yet only a hero’s single step forward can rise above that fate. Now, it’s your turn to defy it. The PlayStation Store page for Vindictus: Defying Fate is now live and you can add the game to your wishlist .

sources.title: Vindictus: Defying Fate Targets 2027 Release on PC and PS5
sources.text: Nexon has released a new cinematic trailer for Vindictus: Defying Fate, giving players another look at the upcoming action RPG. Alongside the trailer, the company confirmed that the game is targeting a 2027 release on PC and PlayStation 5. The new trailer, titled “Let the Righteous Judge,” offers a glimpse at the game’s dark fantasy world and some of the mysteries surrounding its story. Now, the studio isn’t giving too much away just yet, but it does provide a better look at the setting players will eventually get to explore. If you’re unfamiliar with Vindictus: Defying Fate, it’s an action RPG set in a medieval fantasy world. Players will be able to control a “large roster of distinct characters”, each with their own abilities, combos, and fighting styles. Several familiar faces from the series are returning, including Lann, Fiona, Karok, and Delia. They’ll be going up against Fomorian creatures inspired by Celtic mythology, including some seriously massive enemies that will put players’ combat skills to the test. Nexon says the game will combine action-focused combat with RPG progression and character customization, giving players plenty of ways to approach its challenges. There’s still quite a bit we don’t know about Vindictus: Defying Fate, including its exact release date. The game is currently targeting 2027, though its Steam page is already live and its PlayStation Store listing went up on November 12. Players can wishlist the game now on Steam. What do you think of Vindictus: Defying Fate’s latest trailer? Leave your thoughts down in the comments, and join the official Insider Gaming Discord server . sources.text: A Xbox Game Studios e a Playground Games divulgaram um novo vídeo de gameplay de Fable , reboot da tradicional franquia de RPG. A apresentação aconteceu nesta quinta-feira (12), durante as comemorações dos 25 anos do Xbox , e trouxe aproximadamente quatro minutos de uma missão inédita. O vídeo apresenta uma sequência de exploração na região de Deepwood, onde o protagonista investiga acontecimentos mágicos que estão afetando os moradores de Oakshire. O novo Fable tem lançamento previsto para 23 de fevereiro de 2027 , com versões para PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S e PC. A demonstração acompanha o Herói de Briar Hill, protagonista da aventura, ao lado de Arden, um herói local. Os dois entram nas profundezas de Deepwood para investigar fenômenos mágicos que vêm causando problemas aos habitantes de Oakshire. Durante a missão, os personagens encontram uma área onde a magia natural da floresta parece ter sido corrompida por uma força externa. A exploração também revela pistas sobre quem ou o que pode estar por trás dos acontecimentos, estabelecendo um dos mistérios que os jogadores deverão investigar. Segundo a descrição oficial da Xbox Game Studios, a sequência foi preparada especialmente para as comemorações de aniversário da marca. O material oferece uma nova amostra da ambientação de fantasia do RPG, que marca o retorno de uma das franquias mais conhecidas do Xbox. Desenvolvido pela Playground Games, estúdio responsável pela franquia Forza Horizon , o novo Fable representa um reinício da série de RPG criada originalmente pela Lionhead Studios. O jogo está previsto para chegar em 23 de fevereiro de 2027 , nas seguintes plataformas: A chegada ao PlayStation 5 também amplia a disponibilidade da franquia, historicamente associada aos consoles Xbox. Com a nova demonstração, a Microsoft continua apresentando detalhes do retorno de Fable , que terá uma nova interpretação do universo de fantasia de Albion. sources.title: 21 original Xbox games are now on PC via backward compatibility
sources.text: There are now 25 classic Xbox games available on PC, and four have achievements Xbox has added 21 new original Xbox games to its backwards compatibility catalogue on PC. The Elder Scrolls 3: Morrowind, Star Wars Battlefront, Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic, TimeSplitters 2, and more have been added to the catalogue, bringing the roster up to 25 on PC . Four of the games available on the service will also have unlockable achievements. The following games will join the PC backward compatibility catalogue with achievements:Â Star Wars: KOTOR, Star Wars: KOTOR 2, Blinx: The Time Sweeper, and Conker: Live and Reloaded. You can unlock achievements for these games when playing on an Xbox console too. This announcement comes as part of Xbox’s ongoing FanFest. Xbox CEO Asha Sharma also used the event to reveal that id Software is working on its next game after Doom: The Dark Ages . Xbox will also be hoping that this earns it some goodwill in the gaming community, following a year full of layoffs . These layoffs are part of Xbox’s ongoing “reset”, which has seen multiple studios spun off, sold, or merged with others, such as Bethesda and Obsidian , who now work together. Others have seen a massively reduced headcount.

sources.text: Grand Theft Auto VI , o título com o maior número de pré-vendas de todos os tempos na Microsoft Store, será lançado em 19 de novembro. Diante da demanda sem precedentes, recomendamos que todos iniciem a pré-instalação o quanto antes para garantir que estejam prontos para o dia do lançamento. Grand Theft Auto VI poderá ser jogado desde o primeiro dia pelo XBOX Cloud Gaming no XBOX One e no XBOX Series X|S, a partir da 3h da manhã (horário de Brasília). Isso significa que mais jogadores poderão aproveitar um dos jogos mais aguardados do ano nos consoles que já possuem. Ao ser jogado pela nuvem com o XBOX Cloud Gaming, o jogo utiliza as configurações gráficas do XBOX Series S. Estamos animados para levar Grand Theft Auto VI a mais jogadores de XBOX no lançamento. Nos próximos meses, também adicionaremos mais títulos da Rockstar Games ao XBOX Cloud Gaming, incluindo Grand Theft Auto V , Red Dead Redemption 2 e outros. A partir de 11 de novembro, jogadores nos mercados em que o serviço está disponível poderão comprar tempo de jogo na nuvem para jogar títulos compatíveis por streaming sem uma assinatura do Game Pass. A transmissão de Grand Theft Auto VI pela nuvem começa às 3h da manhã (horário de Brasília) de 19 de novembro. Garanta hoje mesmo Grand Theft Auto VI na pré-venda da Microsoft Store . A disponibilidade dos jogos na nuvem, as opções de compra, os dispositivos compatíveis, a elegibilidade das contas e os recursos podem variar de acordo com o mercado e o dispositivo. Grand Theft Auto VI deve ser adquirido separadamente.

sources.name: PC Gamer
sources.title: New Grand Theft Auto 6 trailer is for a TV show that exists within Grand Theft Auto 6
sources.text: Macca and Friends is coming to Weazel TV on November 19. Get ready for some wheels within wheels, as DiscussingFilm has revealed an animated trailer for a Grand Theft Auto 6 TV show—and I don't mean a trailer for a show about GTA 6, but a trailer for a show in GTA 6. Macca and Friends, as the show is known, follows the adventures of a gang of anthropomorphic Floridian—Leonidan, I suppose—animals as they try to find their way in the world, accompanied to some extent by a beefed-up cop. The animals are cops too. It's a bit like Scooby Doo, maybe, but more egalitarian. Rockstar hasn't said anything about the show, but this isn't the first appearance of Macca: A Macca and Friends mural appeared in a real-life BurgerShot that was set up in Miami's Kaseya Center in October, and a billboard for the show was erected in Miami as well. Both advertised Macca and Friends as "coming November 19 on Weazel," a Fox-like television channel that exists within the GTA universe. How much of an actual, full-on show Rockstar has constructed here, I cannot say. Remedy has done similar things with its games, but those are just brief snippets delivering a little bit of meta narrative ; Rockstar, by comparison, gave us multiple stand-up comedy shows in GTA 5 and black-and-white films in Red Dead Redemption 2… not to mention, fully animated horse testicles . In that light, is it hard to believe they may have created an entire animated series for GTA 6? It might just be another blast from the GTA marketing machine—Rockstar is also literally renting the Miami Heat to promote its game, after all. At this point I don't think anything's off the table. PlayStation and Xbox owners will find out in less than a week: Grand Theft Auto 6 launches on November 19. A PC release date (or any kind of PC announcement at all) remains elusive. Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team. GTA 6 guide : Everything we know GTA 6 cars : The garage lineup GTA 6 characters : Your anti-hero cast GTA 6 map : Confirmed Vice City locales GTA 6 PC release : When's it going to happen? Andy has been gaming on PCs from the very beginning, starting as a youngster with text adventures and primitive action games on a cassette-based TRS80. From there he graduated to the glory days of Sierra Online adventures and Microprose sims, ran a local BBS, learned how to build PCs, and developed a longstanding love of RPGs, immersive sims, and shooters. He began writing videogame news in 2007 for The Escapist and somehow managed to avoid getting fired until 2014, when he joined the storied ranks of PC Gamer. He covers all aspects of the industry, from new game announcements and patch notes to legal disputes, Twitch beefs, esports, and Henry Cavill. Lots of Henry Cavill. sources.name: PlayStation Blog
sources.title: The Outer Worlds 2’s first DLC arrives December 2
sources.text: The first in a two-part Side Effects Guaranteed narrative adventure arrives soon, with part two coming spring 2027. The time has come to expand on the experience for The Outer Worlds 2 with the first of a two-part story expansion, Side Effects Guaranteed, arriving on December 2. After a distress signal from a derelict ship is picked up, you and your crew quickly get embroiled into the story of an abandoned settlement, a power struggle for the future of the Sub Rosa criminal organization, and the fate of a team who has been subjected to something that will cause them all to die from explosive cell death. Really, it’s more a liquefaction than explosion, but it means death nonetheless. A brand new story filled with moral quandaries and consequences big and small isn’t the only thing you’ll experience in the first DLC. An Earth Directorate Commander should always be sure to have a weapon at their side, and there are five new weapons to add to the arsenal. Such as the Immobilizer. Think of it like a gun that makes gravity forget to exist around its target, allowing them to float in the air, so you can switch to another weapon and pick them off as you like. Great for combining with grenades for anti-gravity explosions or the Tactical Time Dilation device for slowing down time and getting some critical shots in. There is also the 1/6 Resolver that allows every sixth bullet that is fired from it to pack an extra special punch. For those who built their characters just right, they won’t have to empty the gun every time to get that critical hit, either. Other weapons include a weapon that does additional damage to creatures, a special Tossball Stick, and a new plasma weapon for some energy fun. Yet it isn’t all about the weapons. Side Effects Guaranteed will also bring with it a level cap increase up to 36, new perks, new flaws, and a new Sub Rosa radio station with 20 new songs. There is also the all-new region of Elysium Valley to explore with unique quests and new facilities to make your way through. That’s a lot of new! While the events of the DLC do trigger right before the point of no return in the main game, there is also a way to jump easily into the action. From the main menu if you start a new game, you will see an option to start Side Effects Guaranteed directly. This will load a pre-made character at level 27 that you can assign skill points and perks to so you can experience the DLC however you’d like and get started right away. Not happy with the character you made (or the one you already have)? Coming to everyone at the same time as the release of Side Effects Guaranteed is a new update that will allow players to respec their character at any time. And for those who want more skills to play around with, a new addition to the custom game options allows you to adjust how many skill points you get per level. Find the balance that is right for you. Or become an Earth Director demi-god. Your worlds, your way. But remember, however you decide to deal with Sub Rosa or the subjects of Elysium Valley will have consequences. Side effects, some might say, that will lead directly into the next installment of The Outer Worlds 2 two-part story expansion when it releases in the spring of 2027. Until then, may skill catch you where fortune fails. Side Effects Guaranteed releases on December 2nd or is available in the Premium Edition or Premium Edition Upgrade for The Outer Worlds 2 .

sources.name: Xbox Wire BR
sources.title: Efeitos colaterais estão garantidos no primeiro DLC de The Outer Worlds 2, que chega em 2 de dezembro
sources.text: Um sinal de socorro leva você e sua tripulação da Incognito até uma nave abandonada, onde vocês encontram os tripulantes em animação suspensa. Tudo indica que há algo de errado, especialmente a poça do que muito provavelmente já foi uma pessoa. Você recupera uma mensagem em vídeo deixada pela capitã da nave, que explica que a tripulação foi contaminada por algo durante um roubo e que, se não encontrarem uma cura, isso causará uma morte celular explosiva. E, por morte celular explosiva, ela quer dizer algo mais parecido com uma… “liquefação”. Pelo jeito da poça no chão: é liquefação mesmo. Esse é o cenário para o lançamento da primeira parte de uma expansão narrativa em DLC de The Outer Worlds 2 , dividida em duas partes, em 2 de dezembro. Em Side Effects Guaranteed, a mensagem em vídeo que você encontrou leva até Gordon Hazen, um dos principais agentes da Sub Rosa, uma organização criminosa formada por pessoas que compartilham dos mesmos ideais e escolheram viver roubando das diversas facções em vez de trabalhar para elas. Gordon, por sua vez, envia você para Elysium Valley, uma nova região de Eden que abriga um assentamento de antigos súditos do Protetorado, esquecidos por seus líderes. Ele acredita que eles podem ter as respostas para salvar sua tripulação. Embora prefira a diplomacia à violência, ele precisa que você faça o que for necessário para conseguir as informações de que precisa. Mas Gordon não é o único interessado em Elysium Valley. Outro agente da Sub Rosa, Algernon Lankester, quer recrutar você para ajudá-lo a explorar os súditos em benefício próprio. O destino dos súditos, dos agentes congelados da Sub Rosa e o futuro da própria organização estão nas suas mãos, nosso intrépido Comandante. No entanto, uma nova história não será a única novidade de Side Effects Guaranteed quando o DLC for lançado daqui a algumas semanas. Além de explorar a nova região de Elysium Valley, os jogadores vão encontrar novas ameaças, como canídeos ferozes e sprats primitivos. O que é um sprat primitivo? É só um sprat normal, mas cerca de 100 vezes maior. Com certeza, eles são tão amigáveis quanto seus primos bem menores e vão perdoar todas as vezes em que você atirou neles “sem querer” enquanto explorava Arcadia. Com essas novas ameaças, vem a possibilidade de deixar seu Comandante ainda mais forte e, é claro, com mais defeitos (mas no bom sentido). O limite de nível aumentará de 30 para 36, trazendo mais pontos de habilidade para diversificar sua configuração de personagem. Poder chegar ao nível 36 também significa que você poderá adquirir mais três vantagens, com 15 vantagens inéditas adicionadas às opções disponíveis. Também serão introduzidos quatro novos defeitos que podem mudar a forma de jogar com seu Comandante, como “Lethally Tolerant”, que reconhece sua resistência acumulada a substâncias químicas e aumenta sua toxicidade máxima. Isso é ótimo na hora, mas, se você sofrer um colapso de toxicidade, morrerá instantaneamente. Outro exemplo é “Must Have Been the Wind”, que marca um “alvo de assassinato” em um grupo de combate. Eliminar o alvo concede um bônus de 20% no dano e na velocidade até o fim do combate, mas não conseguir eliminá-lo ou atacar alguém que não seja o alvo aplica ao jogador uma penalidade de 10% no dano e na velocidade por 30 segundos. São recompensas que realmente vêm acompanhadas de grandes riscos. Side Effects Guaranteed também trará novas armas, novas armaduras e novos trajes para cada um dos companheiros, além de uma estação de rádio inédita comandada pela Sub Rosa, com 20 novas músicas para o jogo. Para quem quiser ir direto à ação no DLC, será adicionado um novo ponto de partida alternativo ao menu principal ao selecionar um novo jogo, permitindo começar com um arquivo de jogo salvo personalizado que coloca você no início do DLC. Inicie o jogo, distribua seus pontos de habilidade e de vantagem e aproveite Side Effects Guaranteed sem demora! Essa aventura repleta de conteúdo, com uma história profunda e sistemas para criar seu Comandante ideal, preparará o terreno para o próximo DLC de The Outer Worlds 2 , que chegará no segundo trimestre de 2027. As escolhas que você fizer terão impacto direto no próximo DLC. A primeira parte dessa história que se desenrola ao longo da expansão, Side Effects Guaranteed, será lançada em 2 de dezembro e também está incluída na Edição Premium ou no Upgrade para a Edição Premium de The Outer Worlds 2 .

sources.title: XBOX Playback chegou: reviva sua história com XBOX
sources.text: A partir de hoje, o XBOX Playback reúne os destaques do seu histórico disponível em XBOX, de todas as gerações, em uma experiência personalizada. Pela primeira vez, você pode relembrar e reviver o papel que teve na história de XBOX. Veja quando sua jornada começou, revisite os jogos aos quais você mais dedicou tempo e redescubra conquistas e momentos ao longo do caminho. Seu Playback inclui seu primeiro jogo de XBOX, o tempo total de jogo, o game que você mais jogou, seus anos de maior atividade, sua maior sequência de dias jogando e muito mais. Como não há dois jogadores iguais, cada pessoa terá um Playback diferente. Seja você um veterano que começou a jogar com um controle Duke ou alguém que ligou seu primeiro console neste ano, uma história personalizada estará esperando por você. A partir de hoje, você pode assistir ao seu Playback diretamente no console (procure a opção no painel) ou assistir ao seu vídeo personalizado na web, entrando com sua conta XBOX aqui . Quer se aprofundar um pouco mais? Acesse seu Arquivo do Playback na web para explorar mais do seu histórico disponível. Relembre alguns dos seus primeiros marcos, suas maiores conquistas e muito mais. O XBOX Playback será disponibilizado gradualmente ao longo do dia, então não se preocupe se ele não aparecer de imediato. Depois de assistir ao seu Playback, escaneie o QR code no final do vídeo no console ou selecione “compartilhar” na web para receber seu cartão personalizado do Playback. Compartilhe com amigos ou publique nas redes sociais com a hashtag #XBOXPlayback. O XBOX Playback reúne anos de história de XBOX de uma maneira totalmente nova. Esperamos que o Playback desperte algumas lembranças, surpreenda você ou traga à memória um jogo em que você não pensava há algum tempo. O Playback se baseia nos dados disponíveis da sua conta, por isso algumas partes do seu histórico podem estar incompletas ou demorar para aparecer. O Playback está disponível em 15 países* ( incluindo o Brasil ) a partir de hoje até 31 de dezembro de 2026. Seja você alguém que joga com a gente desde o início ou que está apenas começando, obrigado por fazer parte de XBOX. *Disponível até 31 de dezembro de 2026 na Argentina, Austrália, Brasil, Canadá, Colômbia, França, Alemanha, Hungria, Itália, México, Polônia, África do Sul, Espanha, Reino Unido e Estados Unidos. Requer pelo menos 1 ponto de Gamerscore (pontuação do jogador) em XBOX, 1 Conquista e 1 minuto de jogo válido vinculados ao seu perfil XBOX; o acesso pelo console requer pelo menos 1 minuto de jogo válido no console. Baseado nos dados disponíveis; alguns dados podem estar incompletos ou apresentar atrasos.

stories.title: GDC State of the Game Industry report: 40% of developers are using generative AI for work
stories.summary: 40% of developers are using generative AI in their work, according to the latest State of the Game Industry report from the Game Developers Conference (GDC). Read more

sources.name: GamesIndustry.biz
sources.title: GDC State of the Game Industry report: 40% of developers are using generative AI for work
sources.text: Survey project lead Beth Elderkin lays bare the mood of the industry, the job market, and how people are making games 40% of developers are using generative AI in their work, according to the latest State of the Game Industry report from the Game Developers Conference (GDC). That's an increase of 4% on the previous report, but survey project lead and content marketing manager Beth Elderkin notes that this is a smaller increase than last time. 57% of developers using the tech employ it for text generation, research, early prototyping, coding, and presentations. Generative AI is most popular with business operations and services, mobile-only studios, and free-to-play developers. 27% of AAA workers feel encouraged or pressured to use generative AI; 9% of indie developers say the same. 55% of respondents said that AI is having a negative impact on games, a 1% increase year-on-year; where previously this topic was the subject of larger percentage swings, now it has calmed down. "What appeared to me based on the data is that the technology was not necessarily theoretical, but still early in those first two years," Elderkin tells GamesIndustry.biz . "Last year, for the survey prior to this one, it was more part of the everyday conversation. But in this past year, it has completely changed in terms of what people know about it, how people use it, and how often people use it. So I don't know if the battle lines have been drawn. I think it's more that people just know the technology now, and it's an actuality instead of a theoretical issue, so they know how they want to use it or whether they want to use it at all." 33% of respondents have been laid off in the last 24 months, and around half said that their company had conducted layoffs. 68% of AAA staffers say that their studio has cut jobs, while 35% of respondents from more established studios have made redundancies. For younger indies, this figure is just 14%. 54% of those who have been made redundant have not found another job; 25% say they have applied for at least 100 jobs. Looking at co-development, almost half of respondents work for studios that have used some form of external development in the last 12 months. 16% of staff at non-co-development studios say that their companies have started to offer co-development services as a means of generating extra income or diversifying their portfolio. 50% of respondents say that they had turned to self funding, often "leveraging contract work and co-development" as a means of financing their own projects. On the funding point, Elderkin said that publishers were "expecting more" from developers before giving them financing. "The overall consensus was that publishers are expecting more right out of the gate," she says. "They want your game to have a high number of wishlists and a social media following, and they want it to be in a very good state. You have to get something good enough to present, but you need funding to do that. If you don't have funding, you have to figure out how to self-fund and get yourself to that point. There's also the challenge, especially for indie studios, of having more studios than available funding. We're also seeing private equity investments start to pull back and become more reserved than they were during the pandemic." PC remains dominant for developers, with 81% of respondents saying they are working on their upcoming project for this platform. PlayStation 5 came in at 45%, with Xbox Series X/S at 37%. 10% of respondents are working on projects for the next PlayStation console, while 8% are developing for Xbox's upcoming Project Helix. The number of developers working on virtual reality, augmented reality, and mixed reality projects has collapsed from 8% to 3%. Asked if this is due to the changing focus of Oculus owner Meta, Elderkin says that this "could be part" of the reason why attention has dwindled. "But I also think it's because we're not seeing many new announcements in the field. Steam is coming out with its own offering, so hopefully we'll see some growth in the future. Over the past couple of years, we've heard about VR studios shutting down, including the developers behind Moss, whose games I love. They're beautiful. "Personally, I'm sad to see interest in VR decreasing right now, because I think there's a lot of value in that kind of immersive experience. But until we see more innovation in the space, I don't think people will focus on it. I think they've turned their attention elsewhere." She continues: "As we see a decrease in use, we're also seeing less focus from Meta, Google, and other companies that were pursuing VR more heavily. They're moving away from it, and I think we're seeing the results. Developers don't want to make a game for a platform people aren't using or looking to expand and grow." Looking at engine use, Unreal and Unity came in at 35% and 28%, respectively, but were both down 7% and 2% respectively. This coincides with 23% of respondents saying that they were using a proprietary engine. Crunch and overtime remain issues within the industry; 86% of developers say that they have worked over 40 hours in a week, with nearly half saying they needed or wanted to do this. 16% felt pressured to work longer hours. 8%, however, say they have experienced "mandatory overtime", aka crunch. 63% of respondents say that this overwork could have been avoided, citing poor planning, project changes and leadership. 65% say that their mental health has suffered as a result of their job; 32% say they strongly agree that long hours and layoffs have taken a toll on their mental health. On the topic of unionisation, 15% of US-based respondents are part of a union, a 3% increase year-on-year. 80% support unionisation within the industry, while 55% are interested in joining a union. That's a 7% drop; Elderkin initially suspected this was due to more respondents already being in unions, but in fact it was driven by an increase in respondents who were not i

sources.name: The Verge Games
sources.title: More game developers are starting to use generative AI
sources.text: The GDC Festival of Gaming’s latest annual industry survey shows an increase in AI usage among game developers.﻿ The GDC Festival of Gaming’s latest annual industry survey shows an increase in AI usage among game developers.﻿ More video game developers are using generative AI tools in their jobs compared to last year, according to the GDC Festival of Gaming’s latest annual industry survey . Forty percent of developers surveyed say they use it “as part of their job,” an increase from 36 percent in 2025 . Usage was higher with game developers that work on free-to-play games at 58 percent and mobile-only studio workers at 70 percent. The survey is being published as the game industry continues to reckon with generative AI tools. While many game developers, particularly indie developers , have spoken out strongly against the technology, AI is at the center of indie awards conversations in part because Big Walk developer House House “sparingly” used LLMs to assist with technical challenges in the “final stretch” of development. AI is also increasingly being used to reverse-engineer retro games . And in a post on Thursday , Xbox CEO Asha Sharma seemed to indicate that AI will be central to Xbox’s future, saying that “A small team will be able to build worlds that today demand hundreds of developers and hundreds of millions of dollars.” Seventy three percent of the survey’s respondents said they used AI for research and brainstorming, while 62 percent used it for data analysis and summarization, and 56 percent for code generation and debugging. Twenty two percent of respondents used generative AI for concept art or visual ideation, and 8 percent used it for production art or final game assets. The survey also included grim numbers about layoffs, with 34 percent of respondents saying they have been laid off sometime in the past two years.

sources.name: Eurogamer
sources.title: A new report reckons 40% of developers in the video games industry are using generative AI - but even more think it's harmful
sources.text: "I did not get into a creative industry to hand over the creativity to an algorithm." Despite all the outrage and criticism around game developers and publishers using generative AI in gaming, a new report from the Game Developers Conference (GDC) calculates that as many as 40 percent of developers active in the industry use the controversial tools in their work. This is up four percent compared to the same report last year . That's according to the latest State of the Game Industry report from GDC , which gathers data from more than 2,300 respondents including, but not limited to, game industry professionals, made up of developers, producers, marketers, executives, and investors. The report notes that 57 percent of developers who say they do use it, use gen-AI for "text generation, research, early prototyping, coding, and presentations". There appears to be a big split between triple-A studios that use gen-AI (with 27 percent of triple-A developers noting that they "feel encouraged or pressured" to use it) and indie devs, of which only nine percent say the same. Perhaps unsurprisingly - given how vocally against gen-AI a lot of 'frontline developers' have been - the tools are mostly used by "business operations and services, mobile-only studios, and free-to-play developers". There seems to be a gap in the ages of those willing to use AI tools as well; per the report, over half (54 percent) of people 45 years or older reported using the tools - an eight-point increase from last year's survey. There is also more usage among men (45 percent) than women (33 percent). What is perhaps more striking is that more people responded to the survey saying that they think AI is having a negative impact on games (55 percent) than responded saying they use the tech, suggesting a trend of caution rather than widespread adoption. Notably, respondents saying they are wary of the technology increased one percent since last year, so more people think AI is having a negative effect on the industry now than at the same time in 2025. Perhaps that's because of the sweeping layoffs we've seen across the games industry, often mentioned in the same breath as AI. Or the 'AI slop' that's been flooding Steam and pushing more traditional developers out. Orr some of the abysmal projects we've seen launch that have clearly used gen-AI assets. "I did not get into a creative industry to hand over the creativity to an algorithm," said one respondent from the UK when explaining why they don't use gen-AI tools. "I got into this industry to collaborate with creative people, not to have an advanced chatbot riff on the ideas of someone who was laid off," said another from California. "I believe that no one should have to read what no human has written and shouldn't have to see what no human has created," said yet another from Minnesota. The use of generative AI remains controversial in the games industry, though with big companies like Epic and Microsoft doubling down on the tech, it seems this split between developers that want to embrace it and those that don't is only growing larger.
